title: SilicaGuard instrument regression fixtures
description: Answer profiles with the tier each must produce, per condition. Master Reference v1.0 11.7: the instrument regression suite. Approved by the Clinical Lead on the same pull request as the instrument version it tests, because an expected tier is a clinical statement, not a test detail. The same file is consumed by the Python suite and by the device's JavaScript interpreter, which is what makes 'channels are equivalent' checkable rather than asserted.

instrument.description: The instrument code these fixtures test. Must match the instrument file beside them.

version.description: The instrument version. Fixtures are version-specific: a threshold moving is a new version, and the old fixtures describe the old version's behaviour, which is exactly what makes the change visible.

approved_by.description: The Clinical Lead's name. Required before these fixtures gate a release, because an expected tier is a clinical assertion.

status.description: example is a format illustration and may not gate anything; the test suite skips it for a real instrument and uses it only to exercise the harness.

profiles.description: Each profile is one screening. Aim for coverage of every tier, every safety rule, and the unknown/refused handling, rather than many similar profiles.

name.description: What this profile represents clinically, in the Clinical Lead's words. Read aloud in review, and printed when the test fails.

channel.description: Which channel's question subset applies. A profile that omits a question the channel does not ask is complete, not incomplete (13.1).

answers.description: Question code to recorded answer value. An explicit unknown or refused option belongs here too: an unanswered red-flag question must never read as a negative (12.2 item 10).

previous_answers.description: The same worker's previous screening, where this profile tests deterioration. Omit for a first visit.

expect.description: What the cascade must produce. A profile asserting only the primary tier is weaker than one asserting per-condition tiers, because a two-condition instrument can reach the right primary tier for the wrong reason.

tiers.description: Condition code to the tier that condition must reach.

scored_tiers.description: The tier before deterioration escalation and overrides, per condition. Asserting this as well as the final tier is what distinguishes 'the override fired' from 'the score was already there'.

scores.description: Condition code to expected score. Optional: a score is an implementation detail of the cascade, while a tier is the clinical output.

overrides.description: Safety rule codes that must fire, exactly. An empty list asserts that none do, which is a real assertion and the one most likely to catch an over-eager rule.

deterioration_changed.description: Whether the trajectory comparison must report worsening.

incomplete.description: True where this profile must produce NO tier because an applicable question is unanswered (13.1). Mutually exclusive with every other expectation.
